# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

<!-- cap-evolve:journal-append-below — add your Iteration entry under this line; do not edit anything above it -->

## Iteration cand_0001 — bounded in-body policy guards on the 3 write tools (API-unchecked rules)
- Changes I made (1 line/edit; file + cluster):
  - update_reservation_flights.py: guard raises when a **basic_economy** reservation's flight SEGMENTS (flight_number,date multiset) change; cabin-only change kept allowed. (Cluster: basic-econ flight-change — policy says API does not check.)
  - update_reservation_baggages.py: guard raises when total_baggages < existing (no bag removal), and when nonfree_baggages != max(0,total−free_allowance). (Clusters: bag-removal, wrong derived paid-bag count.)
  - book_reservation.py: guard raises when nonfree_baggages != max(0,total−free_allowance) and when >5 passengers. (Clusters: wrong derived paid-bag count, >5 pax.)
  - Sharpened all three docstrings with the free-bag formula + basic-econ rule + "certificate not allowed for flight change" note.
- Expected effect + why safe: these enforce ONLY policy rules the environment API explicitly does not check; each guard fires ONLY on the exact violating condition, so no gold-consistent action is altered. The free-bag formula was validated against ALL 2000 DB reservations (0 mismatches) → derived-value guards have an empty false-positive set. All 30 traces this iteration are pure INFRA failures (SPA deploy) — no actionable task signal — so this is the "robustness gain, don't regress" move the focus block asked for.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none — seed baseline, LEDGER/RUNMAP empty.
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet.
- Deliberately did NOT guard rules the primitives ALREADY enforce (payment-in-profile, certificate-for-update, gift-card balance, passenger-count-match) — redundant, would add no signal. Skipped the "cabin change after a flown flight" rule (needs flight-status/date reasoning, false-positive risk without trace evidence).
- Plateau signal: n/a (iter 1). If REJECTED because infra still voids the re-score, the guards did not get exercised — not a refutation of their design; iter 2 should keep them and, if a real re-score lands, look at any newly-visible action_check failures.
- Focus next iteration: if traces become real, cluster action_check failures (esp. flight-change payment method, cabin-change-price refund/charge direction) and add bounded guards; consider the flown-flight cabin rule only with trace evidence.
